For those naysayers who said milling decks would never win games...:

Brinksmanship
Political Action
Political Card - Worth 1 vote
Called by any Vampire at +1 stealth
If this referendum is successful, put this card in play. Any
Methuselah who has exhausted his or her library and begins his or her
untap phase with less than a full handmust attempt to withdraw. On
that Methuselah's next untap phase, if the withdrawal fails, that
Methuselah is ousted. If any Methuselah successfully withdraws, you
are ousted.

I see Egotha + Christianus, using Slaughterhouses, Feline Sabouteurs,
and perhaps obf weenies for the all new Border Skirmishes...

Your thoughts?

Messages.Author: Hollowboy
Messages.Body:
ped_...@hotmail.com (Ped Xing) wrote in message news:<51ecf271.03052...@posting.google.com>...


Basically, yes, I agree, that strategy is now looking a whole lot
stronger.

I can see a few downfalls to avoid:

1) Staying alive. too much milling in your deck, and you have no
defence, so you get ousted after crippling your prey, and everyone
hates you :(

2) Backstreaming from prey - milling is annoying. You get attacked a
lot for doing it. Luckily, HoS are capable of defending like big scary
defendey kinda guys.

3) Passing votes - sure, the HoS *can* do it (particularly if paired
with the !ven), but other players will expect to see Brinkmanship in
your deck, and might save their hosers / intercept up for it...
Delaying Tactics, cross table players lending your predator use of
their intercept locations, stuff like that.

4) Successful withdraws! Your prey might plot against you by hoarding
redirections etc to allow a withdrawl, so you better have a sure way
to cause pool loss / blood loss / combat in that turn. Society of
Leopols / Anarch Revolt would fit the bill... tons of things would. I
guess the point to this one is don't focus too hard on the milling,
with bleed as your only other offence, or you might get thwarted at
the last minute.

---

As to the nuts-and-bolts of using this, personally, I would just
include Brinking and milling as an angle, and not focus the whole deck
there. I would instead play strategy X, with Slaughterhouse milling
happening quietly in the background, to essentially have two offences
going simultaneously.

X for me would probably be a crossover with the !ven, and their
+strength brutes, either vote-based, or something dirty with Society
of Leopold and intercept.

Turn one:
Parthenon
Bring out Krid

Turn 2:
Lupine Assualt
Dimple Clan impesonates

Total Mill: 5 cards

Turn 3:
2x Slaughterhouses (mill 4 cards)
Krid Hunts
Bring out Ellison Humboldt

Total Mill: 9 cards

Feline Sab (mill 5 cards)
Krid does something
Influence another Prince

Total Mill: 29 cards

Krid does something

Total Mill: 57 cards

Turn 7: 1x Slaughterhouse (mill 20 cards)
Minion Tap
Something else
Feline Sab x2 (mill 10 cards)
Krid does something

Total Mill: 87 cards

Assuming your prey actually plays more than 3 cards in 7 turns, that's
them on the ropes.

You play one card, everyone else looses one card. So basically, you
waste all your card slots forcing people to discard. 90 cards played
by you = 90 cards lost by everyone else.

How do you expect to:

1) Force a vote through with a pile of untitled Anarchs (don't say
"Fee Stake" or "Presence Mods" coz you don't have the card slots).

2) Get rid of everyone's pool and (more importantly) stop other
methusulas being ousted in the 80+ actions you'll need to generate to
mill the table (don't say Life Boon,you don't have the card slots)

3) Stop yourself being ousted in the 80+ actions it will take to mill
the table (don't say bleed bounce or intercept, you don't have the
card slots - and no slots for combat if you get hold of people)

4) Stop everyone else from laughing themselves silly as you attempt to
take 80+ actions to mill the table.

Answers on a postcard

:)

Border Skirmish is something to irritate people, but not a game winner
per se. Maybe (just maybe) if you had either Pochtli or Waste
Management Ops you could stack up and devote, say, 40 card slots to
Border Skirmishes, but hey! There's still that irritating "vote"
problem...

DH
